class.name: WaterMaterial
class.brief_description: Water for any mesh: waves, depth, foam, rain and flow.
class.description: Give it to a lake's plane, a river's ribbon or a [Water3D]. Its waves are a few Gerstner waves rolling along [member wave_direction], or along a [Weather3D]'s wind with [member follow_wind], higher in a stronger wind. What's under the surface is seen through it, bent by the waves ([member refraction]) and fading into [member deep_color] the deeper it is: after [member clarity] meters, what's below is [member color] times as bright. Foam gathers along shores and on steep crests, rain ripples the surface, and with [member flow] the surface moves like a river's. The waves stay put when [WorldOrigin] shifts the world. [method get_height_at] gives their height on the CPU, for boats and things that float. It needs the Forward+ or Mobile renderer, and draws in the transparent pass, after what's under it.

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: How far above (or below) the still surface the waves are at [param map_position] (a map position's x and z: global plus [member WorldOrigin.offset]), now, as the shader moves the surface there.

members.member: How sharp the crests are, from [code]0[/code] (round swells) to [code]1[/code] (pointed crests, where foam gathers).
How clear the water is: after this many meters, what's below is [member color] times as bright.
What the water does to the light through it, after [member clarity] meters: a pale blue-green keeps the blues and greens and loses the reds.
The water's own color where it's deep, lit by the scene.
How fast the surface moves across the world, in meters a second, for rivers and streams.
How much foam gathers along shores and on crests, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].
If [code]true[/code], the waves roll along a [Weather3D]'s wind and grow with it; otherwise along [member wave_direction] at [member wave_height].
How much the waves bend what's seen through them.
How rough the surface is: low values reflect the sky sharply.
Which way the waves roll across the world (x east, y south), without [member follow_wind].
How high the highest waves are, crest to trough, in meters. With [member follow_wind], it's scaled by the wind's strength.
How far apart the longest waves' crests are, in meters.
